name: tablepro
title: TablePro
description: Open and search your TablePro database connections, browse schema, and run queries.
author: ngoquocdat

commands.name: search-connections
commands.title: Search Connections
commands.description: Search and open saved TablePro connections.

commands.name: menu-bar-connections
commands.title: TablePro Menu Bar
commands.description: Show connections in the menu bar.

commands.name: search-schema
commands.title: Search Schema
commands.description: Search databases and schemas across your connections.

commands.name: recent-tabs
commands.title: Recent Tabs
commands.description: Show recently opened tabs in TablePro.

commands.name: run-query

tools.name: list-connections
tools.title: List Connections
tools.description: List all saved TablePro database connections.

tools.name: list-databases
tools.title: List Databases

tools.name: list-schemas
tools.title: List Schemas

tools.name: list-tables
tools.title: List Tables
tools.description: List tables in a database or schema.

tools.name: describe-table
tools.title: Describe Table
tools.description: Return the column list, types, and constraints for a table.

tools.name: get-table-ddl
tools.title: Get Table DDL

tools.name: run-query
tools.title: Run Query
tools.description: Run a read or write SQL query. Mutating queries require user confirmation.

tools.name: explain-query
tools.title: Explain Query
tools.description: Run EXPLAIN on a query and return the plan.

tools.name: open-connection-window
tools.title: Open Connection in TablePro
tools.description: Open a TablePro connection window so the user can continue work in the GUI.

tools.name: search-history
tools.title: Search Query History
tools.description: Search the saved TablePro query history by text.

ai.instructions: TablePro is a native macOS database client. Use list-connections to find a connection by user description, then pass its UUID to other tools. Always describe-table before generating queries against an unknown schema. For mutating SQL (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, ALTER, TRUNCATE, MERGE) the run-query tool will require user confirmation, never bypass that. The connection's external-access setting may reject your query as read-only, surface that error to the user verbatim. Prefer open-connection-window when the user wants to inspect or edit data interactively rather than streaming rows in chat.

@tablepro open my prod connection in TablePro
